subject: Volume slab bridge and competitive clauses for CloudPort deal
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha@cloudport.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial proposal — volume slab bridge and migration credits

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for taking time to demo last week. Per our conversation I attached an updated pricing ladder and a short migration playbook. Topline proposal: we can offer a conditional per-token match against the commercial rates you shared from your incumbent for an initial period, coupled with one-time migration credits to cover integration and token delta.

Key points in the attachment (CloudPort_MAProposal_v2.pdf):
- 12-month minimum term recommended to make the credits/cost work.
- First 90 days: per-token parity to the incumbent (provided you commit to the tier floor).
- Months 4–12: staged slab discounts (see sheet) that improve with higher sustained usage.
- Service: US region, 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for hosted API, standard SLO credits for breaches.

Questions for you: can procurement confirm the exact per-token comparators (model names + effective token rates) so our finance/legal teams can mirror them in the redline? Also, do you require Net 60 billing (we can accommodate but need to run it by finance)?

I copied Karthik for pricing/legal coordination. If this looks directionally right I can ask Ben to prepare a short 90-day parity amendment plus the tier ladder spreadsheet for your legal team.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: CloudPort_MAProposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 14 pages)
From: Aisha Shah <aisha@cloudport.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudPort Procurement <procurement@cloudport.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal — volume slab bridge and migration credits

Vanessa,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposal. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering after an initial review:

- Competitor comparator: OpenAI is offering a limited promo at $0.0004/token for embeddings and $0.0006/token for standard gen over a 6-month window; Anthropic has a multi-month credit for top-of-funnel usage. We need firm parity to OpenAI's promo for the first 6 months to hand this to our product team.
- Commitment floor: we need clarity on the minimum committed tokens/month to qualify for parity.
- Early termination: we need a usage-protected exit if the offering materially underperforms for latency or if model quality regressions occur.
- Billing: procurement prefers Net 60.

Also ask: can you provide the rate comparison sheet (per model) and a migration runbook (how you will route traffic, prefix caching approach, and KV warm-up expectations)?

If you can send a short (≤2 page) amendment that guarantees parity for 6 months with defined metrics, procurement can run an expedited review.

Thanks,
Aisha Shah
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudPort
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha@cloudport.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal — volume slab bridge and migration credits

Aisha — thanks for the clarity. A few counter-proposals from our side to balance commercial risk:

1) Parity window: we can guarantee per-token parity to the OpenAI promo rates you shared, but conditioned on a 12-month committed minimum (total committed tokens for the 12 months). The parity would run for the first 90 days; months 4–12 revert to the staged slab rate but with an overall blended effective price not worse than the incumbent at your historic monthly run-rate.

2) Minimums and shortfall credits: if actual usage falls below the agreed monthly floor we will credit the difference (shortfall credit) back to your account on a pro-rated basis.

3) Termination and SLA: include a performance escape clause — if we miss the agreed latency SLO (p95 > threshold) or availability < 99.5% for two consecutive months, CloudPort can terminate without penalty and receive an applied credit.

4) Migration: we will provide a migration playbook and prefix caching plan (see attached redwood-rate-comparison.xlsx for expected token delta and cost modeling). We will also assign an SRE to coordinate the cutover and KV warming.

5) Billing: Net 60 is acceptable.

We are avoiding a full-match-for-12-months because that materially increases our economics risk on transient promos. The 90-day parity + 9 months blended slab tries to meet both needs. If CloudPort needs an extended parity window we can consider a revenue-share style rebate instead of extending parity.

Attached: redwood-rate-comparison.xlsx (model-level rate comparison, simulation tab).

-Karthik
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha@cloudport.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Suggested structured bridge: 90-day parity + tiered commit

Aisha — quick note on a pragmatic pathway that has closed with other customers:

- Offer: 90 days of immediate per-token parity to the incumbent promo on the models you specified.
- Follow-up: 9 months of tiered pricing with 3 breakpoints (base, growth, scale). If you hit the growth breakpoint we will retroactively rebate the first 90 days to a deeper effective rate.
- Safeguards: 30-day SLA remediation plan, quarterly business reviews, and a defined migration playbook (standard engagement).

Example: if CloudPort commits to 300B tokens over 12 months we set 3 monthly floors and a graduated discount schedule. I've attached the spreadsheet for concrete numbers.

From: Aisha Shah <aisha@cloudport.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suggested structured bridge: 90-day parity + tiered commit

Thanks Ben — the structure is sensible, but procurement/legal have two asks before we can move to signatures:

1) Parity duration: procurement insists on parity for the first 6 months, not 90 days, because the incumbent's promo runs 6 months and our finance model assumes rate parity for that window. If you can do 6 months parity in exchange for the 12-month commit (with the same shortfall credit), we are closer.

2) Early termination credits: we need an explicit schedule that outlines the credit amount if usage is below committed floors or if performance issues trigger an exit.

3) Legal redlines: please provide a short amendment with the parity window, commit floors, shortfall credit language and the SLA escape clause.

Also, can you confirm any restrictions on model versions (i.e., will you guarantee comparable model architecture families for the parity promise)?

If you can send updated language today we will fast-track to legal. Net 60 billing and migration SRE cover are both acceptable.

Regards,
Aisha
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha@cloudport.com>, CloudPort Procurement <procurement@cloudport.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final commercial approach: Bridge & Match offer (summary and next steps)

Aisha — thank you for the candid asks. Below is a concise commercial path we are prepared to take internally to close quickly. If this is acceptable please confirm and we will produce the amendment + PO instructions.

Bridge & Match (summary):
- Term: 12 months committed.
- Parity: Per-token parity to OpenAI promo rates for the first 3 months guaranteed, then a 3-month optional extension to reach parity for month 4–6 if CloudPort achieves agreed growth breakpoints (we're offering this as a conditional bridge rather than unconditional 6 months).
- Pricing months 4–12: tiered slab with retroactive rebate mechanism if growth breakpoints are met (concrete numbers in the spreadsheet).
- Shortfall credits: pro-rated credit applied monthly if usage < committed floor.
- Termination: SLA escape clause — failure to meet agreed latency/availability for two consecutive months permits termination with a defined credit schedule.
- Migration: dedicated SRE, KV warm-up plan, and a production-run playbook.
- Billing: Net 60.

Why this is different: we are providing a conditional path to match the incumbent while protecting economics for both parties — extended unconditional parity materially shifts risk to Redwood for transient promos. We believe the conditional extension balances both needs and delivers a fast migration path for CloudPort.

Next steps: if CloudPort signs off on the Bridge & Match summary we will:
1) Produce a 2-page amendment reflecting parity window, commit floors, shortfall credit schedule and SLA escape clause.
2) Share a PO template and final rate table (redwood-rate-comparison.xlsx).
3) Schedule legal to legal and the SRE kickoff call.

Link to deal and materials: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/CLP-4789 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD_example_link

Please confirm on reply and we will route to legal.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: CloudPort_MAProposal_v2.pdf, redwood-rate-comparison.xlsx
